content.caseIdentity: Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli, (2006) 4 SCC 558
content.facts: Prolonged mutual hostility, separation, and a complete breakdown of the marital relationship over many years.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether such prolonged hostility and separation can justify a decree of divorce on the ground of cruelty under s. 13(1)(ia).
content.ratioDecidendi: Prolonged mutual hostility and separation can constitute mental cruelty. Where the marriage has broken down beyond repair, the Court may grant divorce on the ground of cruelty. Irretrievable breakdown, while not an independent statutory ground, is a relevant consideration in assessing cruelty.
content.holding: Divorce granted on the ground of cruelty; recommendation made for legislative recognition of irretrievable breakdown.
content.relevance: Leading modern authority on mental cruelty under s. 13(1)(ia) and the relevance of irretrievable breakdown within that ground.
